## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.

5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.

## Problem

The `wl sync` command uses a binary author-identity gate: it either allows ALL commits from the configured user.email or rejects them all. When syncing against a remote with commits from a different author identity (e.g., a different email address), sync fails with a hard error.

This is annoying for single-operator repos with multiple machines/emails (false positives) and does not scale for team or CI scenarios.

## Proposed Solution

Replace the binary allow/deny gate with a configurable **author whitelist** (`syncAllowedAuthors`) in `.worklog/worklog.yaml`:

- **Empty list (default)** - same behavior as now: only accept commits from the local user.email (strictest, no change to current security posture)
- **Non-empty list** - accept commits from any email in the whitelist
- **null or true** - allow any author (current --allow-foreign-author behavior)

### Example config

Empty list (default / most secure):
  syncAllowedAuthors: []

Allow specific additional authors:
  syncAllowedAuthors:
    - sorra@thewizardscode.com
    - alice@company.com

Allow all (explicit opt-in):
  syncAllowedAuthors: null

### Implementation points

1. Add syncAllowedAuthors to worklog config schema (in config.defaults.yaml and validation)
2. Modify the sync author-check logic to read syncAllowedAuthors from config, check commit author email against the list
3. Update --allow-foreign-author CLI flag to set/override the config value
4. Update help text and docs to explain the whitelist model
5. Add tests covering: empty list, non-empty list, null/true, mismatch

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New syncAllowedAuthors config key accepted and validated
- [ ] Default empty list enforces current behavior (only local author)
- [ ] Non-empty whitelist allows commits from listed emails
- [ ] Null/true allows all authors (equivalent to current --allow-foreign-author)
- [ ] --allow-foreign-author flag still works (sets config to null or true)
- [ ] Tests: empty list, non-empty list, null/true, author mismatch rejection
- [ ] Help text explains the whitelist model
- [ ] Existing --allow-foreign-author users are unaffected
data.title: Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist

# wl sync reports success while the remote is missing records

## Problem statement

`wl sync` reports "✓ Sync completed successfully" (with "No changes to sync — skipping export and push" / "Work items unchanged: 124") while the **remote git ref (`refs/worklog/data`) is missing ~102 of the local 124 work items**, including every `in_review` item. A fresh checkout on another machine (`wl init` + `wl sync`) therefore only receives the ~22 records present on the remote tip, silently losing work items.

## Users

- **Operators / agents working across multiple machines** — believe their worklog is safely synced to git and mirrored elsewhere, when it is not. Items created on one machine never reach the remote or other clones.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Machine A has a worklog with 124 work items (incl. 44 `in_review`) and a remote ref whose tip contains only 22 workitems (e.g. after a foreign-author full snapshot `27974ce` with 22 records overwrote a 769-record state `768e140`).
2. Run `wl sync` on machine A.
   - Observed: local state 124 items; remote state 22 items; `Work items added: 0`, `Work items unchanged: 124`, then `No changes to sync — skipping export and push` and `✓ Sync completed successfully`. Exit code 0.
3. Run `wl sync` on a fresh checkout (machine B): only ~22 items appear; all `in_review` items are missing.

## Root cause analysis

The delta-sync export (`exportForSync`, `countDirtyRecords`) decides what to export purely from **per-type watermarks** stored in `last_export_timestamps`:

- `workitems` watermark: `2026-08-30T23:17:08.349Z`
- max local `updatedAt`: `2026-08-30T23:14:22.345Z` → **0 records newer than the watermark → `countDirtyRecords().total === 0`** → the §5.4 zero-change fast path skips export+push entirely.

The watermark was advanced by a successful push (of a *delta* containing only the 22 merged remote records), so afterwards **every remaining local record is older than the watermark and is treated as "already synced" — even though the remote never received it**. There is **no reconciliation**: sync never verifies that records older than the watermark actually exist on the remote tip. Once the remote diverges (foreign-author commit, force-push, full snapshot from a different store with fewer records, or a delta/legacy snapshot mismatch), the local-only records become **permanently unpushable** while sync reports success.

Contributing issue: `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` merged the 22 remote records and pushed a *delta of only those 22 records*, not a full snapshot of all 124 — so the 102 missing items were still not exported, yet sync again reported success.

## Expected behaviour

- Sync detects divergence between local and remote beyond the watermark heuristic (e.g. when the local store has records absent from the remote tip), and either exports them (full re-snapshot / reconcile) or fails loudly.
- Sync never reports "✓ Sync completed successfully" / "No changes to sync" when the remote tip is missing records the local store holds.
- A fresh `wl init` + `wl sync` on another machine must reproduce the full worklog state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Divergence detection:** `wl sync` fails (or warns with non-zero exit) when the local store contains work items/comments absent from the remote tip, instead of reporting success.
- [ ] **AC2 — Self-healing export:** When divergence is detected, sync exports the missing records (full snapshot or targeted reconcile) so the remote tip converges to the local state.
- [ ] **AC3 — No false success:** `wl sync` exit code and message reflect whether the remote tip actually converged; "No changes to sync" is only emitted when local and remote are provably identical.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression test:** A test reproduces: local store with records older than the watermark + remote tip missing those records → sync must not report success and must push the records.

## Evidence (AI_Hell repo, 2026-08-30)

- `wl sync --no-push`: `Local state: 124 work items, 583 comments` / `Remote state: 22 work items, 0 comments` / `Work items unchanged: 124` / `No changes to sync — skipping export (--no-push)` / `✓ Sync completed successfully`.
- `git show refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` at tip `1918bdd` → 22 `workitem` records (`kind: delta`).
- Local SQLite: 124 workitems; `last_export_timestamps.workitems = 2026-08-30T23:17:08.349Z`; `MAX(updatedAt) = 2026-08-30T23:14:22.345Z`; records newer than watermark: 0.
- Remote ref history shows the divergence origin: `768e140` full (769 records, 16:30) → … → `27974ce` full (22 records, 23:28) → deltas (22 records each). The 22-record full snapshot supersedes the 769-record one, so fresh clones replay from `27974ce` and get only 22 items.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB — author-identity gate (`--allow-foreign-author`), the flag that unblocks the merge but does not repair the remote.
- WL-0MT2KY0RQ008F50Q / WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q — delta-sync design / §5.4 zero-change fast path; the watermark logic at fault.
- WL-0MT2KZ5GJ000OJIP — remote delta-chain replay (full-snapshot fallback for fresh clones); replay anchor (`27974ce`) is a smaller full snapshot, which is why fresh clones miss records.
data.title: wl sync reports success while remote is missing records — zero-change fast path skips export

# Author-identity gate refusal must surface at default verbosity and exit non-zero (no silent success)

## Problem statement

When the author-identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) refuses to merge foreign-authored worklog commits, `wl sync` at **default verbosity can still report success** ("✓ Sync completed successfully", exit code 0). The refusal is only visible with `--verbose` / `--dry-run`. This is a second facet of the false-success bug in WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS, on a different code path.

## Users

- **Operators running `wl sync` across machines with different git identities** — believe the merge/push succeeded when it was actually refused, so work items silently never reach the remote.

## Steps to reproduce (AI_Hell repo, 2026-08-30)

1. Remote tracking ref contains commits authored by an identity different from the store's configured `user.email` (observed: `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` vs `sorra@thewizardscode.com`).
2. Run `wl sync` (default verbosity).
   - Observed: `✓ Sync completed successfully`, exit 0 — no mention of the gate.
3. Run `wl sync --verbose` or `wl sync --dry-run --json`.
   - Observed: `✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 2 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.` (`d48a703`, `1db5d45`).

## Expected behaviour

- A gate refusal is a **failure**: `wl sync` exits non-zero and prints the refusal reason at default verbosity (no `--verbose` required).
- The message names the offending commits and the expected vs actual author identities, and suggests `--allow-foreign-author` or a config fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Non-zero exit:** `wl sync` exits non-zero when the author-identity gate refuses the merge.
- [ ] **AC2 — Default-verbosity message:** The refusal (offending commits + expected/actual identities) is printed without `--verbose`/`--dry-run`.
- [ ] **AC3 — No false success:** The word "success" / exit 0 is never emitted for a gate-refused sync.
- [ ] **AC4 — Suggestion:** Output suggests `--allow-foreign-author` or the `syncAllowForeignAuthor` config option.
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression test:** Test where remote commits are foreign-authored → assert non-zero exit + refusal text at default verbosity.

## Related work

- WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS — parent bug: "wl sync reports success while remote is missing records — zero-change fast path skips export" (this is the gate-path facet).
- WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB — the author-identity gate itself (`--allow-foreign-author` flag).

# Recovery path for already-diverged worklog repos (doctor command or documented procedure)

## Problem statement

WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS addresses *future* syncs (detection + self-healing + no false success), but repositories that have **already diverged** cannot currently be repaired through a supported path. Observed 2026-08-30:

- **AI_Hell** (`/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell`): remote `refs/worklog/data` tip holds 22 workitems while the local SQLite store has 124 (incl. 44 `in_review`). The zero-change fast path refuses to export (all local records are older than the watermark), so the missing items are permanently unpushable via `wl sync`.
- **ContextHub** (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`): remote held 1 workitem vs 2968 locally before a manual `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` recovered it (pushed 13,590 new JSONL records).

There is no documented escape hatch for "local store has records the remote never received" — the operator must improvise (forcing a full snapshot, `--allow-foreign-author`, manual ref rewrites). This item delivers a supported recovery path.

## Users

- **Operators / agents** whose worklog remote diverged from the local store (foreign-author overwrite, force-push, smaller full snapshot superseding a larger one, or delta/legacy snapshot mismatch) — need a safe, supported way to converge the remote to the local state without data loss.

## Proposed solution

Extend `wl doctor` (or add a dedicated `wl sync --force-full` / `--repair` mode) that:

1. Detects the divergence: local records absent from the remote tip (compare record IDs, not just watermarks).
2. Emits a **full snapshot** of the local store (newest full snapshot on the chain — fixes the replay anchor for fresh clones too, per AC5 of WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS).
3. Pushes with an explicit confirmation/guard so it cannot accidentally overwrite a *larger* remote (safety check: refuse if remote has records the local lacks, unless `--force`).
4. Also resets/clears invalid watermarks if they are the block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Command/mode exists:** A supported command or mode (e.g. `wl doctor resync --full --allow-lossless` or `wl sync --force-full`) that publishes a full snapshot of the local store to the remote ref.
- [ ] **AC2 — Divergence report:** Before pushing, it reports the counts: local records, remote-tip records, records local-only, records remote-only.
- [ ] **AC3 — Lossless guard:** If the remote contains records absent locally, it refuses (or requires an explicit `--force` / `--allow-foreign-author` escalation). No silent data loss.
- [ ] **AC4 — Watermark repair:** If outdated watermarks block export, it resets them so the full snapshot is actually published.
- [ ] **AC5 — Fresh-clone verification:** After the repair, a fresh `wl init` + `wl sync` on another machine reconstructs the full local record set (this also satisfies AC5 of WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** The recovery procedure (and when to use it) is documented in the sync/doctor docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression test:** Test: local store with records older than watermark + remote tip missing them → repair command converges the remote, and a subsequent `wl sync` reports no divergence.

## Evidence (AI_Hell repo, 2026-08-30)

- Local: 124 workitems; `last_export_timestamps.workitems = 2026-08-30T23:17:08.349Z`; `MAX(updatedAt) = 2026-08-30T23:14:22.345Z`; 0 records newer than watermark → `wl sync` fast-path skips export entirely.
- Remote tip `1918bdd` (delta): 22 `workitem` records.
- Fresh clone replays from newest full snapshot `27974ce` (22 records) → only 22 items, all `in_review` items missing.

## Related work

- WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS — parent bug: false-success sync + missing remote records; this item is the *recovery* half of that problem.
- WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS AC4/AC5 — regression coverage that this command must satisfy.
- WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB — author-identity gate; foreign-authored remote histories are a common cause of divergence.
- WL-0MT2KZ5GJ000OJIP — remote delta-chain replay; the full-snapshot anchor logic a repair must respect.
- discovered-from:WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS

# Intake Brief — Boost audit-backed items in wl next sorting (WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5)

## Problem statement

`wl next` and the automatic `reSort` scoring currently rank work without considering whether an audit has been performed. An audit that is `not ready to close` signals that substantive work has been done and the item needs iteration, yet those items compete equally with untouched items that have never been audited. This causes nearly-complete work to slip behind fresh untouched items (of equal or higher base priority), delaying iteration. A deliberate boost for audit-backed, not-ready-to-close items — second only to `critical` priority — is needed.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI selection list** who pick the next item to work on.
  - *As a developer, when I have audited an item and it is not yet ready to close, I want it to appear ahead of any unaudited non-critical item in `wl next`, so iteration on in-progress work is prioritized over starting new untouched work.*
- **Producers / reviewers triaging `wl next -n N`** who scan the grouped list for next actions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit-not-ready boost in scoring:** Items that have an `audit_results` row with `ready_to_close = false` receive a score boost during `reSort`/`computeScore` (and any equivalent ordering path) such that, after `wl re-sort` or auto `reSort` triggered by `wl next`, every non-critical audited-not-ready item is ordered before every unaudited (or audit-ready-to-close) non-critical item, regardless of base priority (high/medium/low) and regardless of age/effort/recency tie-breakers. `critical` items remain strictly ahead of audited-not-ready items even if unaudited.
2. **No boost for ready-to-close or missing audit:** Items with no audit row, or with `ready_to_close = true`, receive no audit boost and retain their existing score. Stale audits (where `auditedAt < updatedAt`) are treated as not boosted — only a fresh audit (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) that is not ready counts — unless explicitly decided otherwise during implementation (document the chosen freshness rule).
3. **`wl next` reflects the boosted order:** `wl next -n N` (with and without `--no-re-sort`) returns items in the same boosted order; `wl next --json` preserves the order; when all `sortIndex` values are equal the fallback `selectBySortIndex` tie-break also respects the audit boost before falling back to effective priority/age.
4. **Critical exemption preserved:** No non-critical item, even with an audit-not-ready boost, outranks a `critical` priority item. The existing Critical Group ordering in `src/commands/grouping.ts` / `packages/shared` remains unchanged.
5. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (including existing `reSort` and `findNextWorkItem` tests).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README/CLI docs, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Only `ready_to_close = false` audits qualify; `true` or absent audits do not boost.
- `critical` priority is never overtaken by the audit boost (hard tier boundary).
- No new external dependencies; change is confined to scoring/sorting logic.
- Must not regress performance of `wl next` or `reSort` on large datasets; audit lookups should use existing `getAuditResult` / cached maps, not per-item N+1 queries without caching.
- Backward compatible: no CLI flag changes required; existing `wl next` flags continue to work.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore()` / `sortItemsByScore()` / `reSort()`** — Score drives `sortIndex` via `getAllOrderedByScore()`. Weights: priority 1000, in_review 600, blocks-high-priority 500, etc. No audit awareness.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:findNextWorkItemFromItems()` / `selectBySortIndex()`** — Selection uses `sortIndex` order; when all `sortIndex` equal, falls back to effective priority then `createdAt`. No audit tie-break.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `audit_results` table** — `saveAuditResult`, `getAuditResult`, `getAllAuditResults`. `wl next` already enriches items with `auditResult` for display but does not use it for ordering.
- **`src/commands/grouping.ts:assignItemGroups()`** — Critical items in `Critical Group N`; remaining groups by stage/file-path. Audit does not affect grouping (by design).
- **TUI selection list** consumes `wl next --json` ordering; boosting `computeScore` automatically benefits the TUI.

## Desired change

1. Extend `computeScore()` (and the parallel `selectBySortIndex` fallback path, if needed) to apply an **audit-not-ready boost** when `store.getAuditResult(id)` (or a batch-fetched map / `EdgeCache`-style cache) returns `readyToClose === false` and the audit is fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`). The boost must be large enough to outrank any non-critical base priority difference (e.g., tiered comparison or numeric boost > 2000 so `low` + boost > `high` unaudited). Keep `critical` (4000) strictly above `high`+boost.
2. Thread the audit freshness check through `sortItemsByScore` / `getAllOrderedByScore` efficiently (batch map, not per-item uncached query in the hot loop).
3. Ensure `findNextWorkItemFromItems` fallback ordering also respects the same audit tier when `sortIndex` values are uniform.
4. Add/adjust unit tests for `database.test.ts` / `persistent-store` covering: audited-not-ready outranks unaudited high, critical outranks audited, ready-to-close gets no boost, missing audit gets no boost, stale audit handling.
5. Update docs/comments (`docs/`, `CLI.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` if needed) to describe the new audit boost tier.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `computeScore()`, `sortItemsByScore()`, `getAllOrderedByScore()`, `reSort()`, `findNextWorkItemFromItems()`, `selectBySortIndex()`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `audit_results` table helpers (`getAuditResult`, `getAllAuditResults`) for efficient audit lookup.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — Verify no grouping change needed; critical tier stays top (reference only).
- `src/commands/next.ts` — Enriches `auditResult` for display; ordering comes from DB layer (reference).
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` if present) — Add reSort/next ordering tests for audit boost.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — This item (audit boost).
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore` weights** — Existing priority/in_review/blocks-high-priority scoring to be extended.
- **`audit_results` table (WL-0MPZNJVWT000IKG7)** — Sole source of truth for audit state; `wl next` already displays audit icons via this table.
- **Critical Group feature (`src/commands/grouping.ts`)** — Establishes precedent for a hard tier (critical) that must remain above the new audit tier.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Boost magnitude risk:** A modest numeric boost (e.g., +600 like in_review) would not outrank a higher priority unaudited item, violating "ahead of any non-critical unaudited". **Mitigation:** Implement as tiered comparison (audit-not-ready tier outranks unaudited tier) or numeric boost > max priority delta (>2000) and cover with tests.
- **Stale audit risk:** Audits older than the work item's `updatedAt` may no longer reflect current work. **Assumption:** Only fresh audits (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) qualify for the boost; stale audits are treated as no-audit. Record final decision in implementation and document it. If the producer prefers stale audits to still boost, adjust before implementation.
- **Performance risk:** Per-item `getAuditResult` in the sort comparator could be N+1. **Mitigation:** Build a `Map<id, AuditResult>` once per `sortItemsByScore` / `reSort` call and reuse, mirroring `EdgeCache` pattern.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable boost, per-priority audit tiers, or grouping changes. **Mitigation:** File separate work items; keep this item to a single audit-not-ready tier second only to critical.
- **Assumption:** `ready_to_close = true` items are typically `in_review` and already receive an in_review boost; they should not receive the additional audit-not-ready boost.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should an audit with `ready_to_close = true` also receive the boost, or only `false`? — Answer (seed intent): Only `not ready to close` (false) should be boosted — ready items are already terminal/in_review and do not need iteration priority. Source: work-item description ("have an audit on file but that are not ready to close").
- Q: Should `critical` items be overtaken by a lower-priority audited item? — Answer (seed intent): No — "ahead of any item (other than critical) that have no audit" implies critical remains on top regardless of audit. Source: work-item description.
- Q: Should stale audits (`auditedAt < updatedAt`) still count for the boost? — Answer (assumption, to be confirmed in implementation): No — only fresh audits (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) qualify; stale audits are treated as no audit for ordering. Rationale: edited work invalidates prior audit signal. Open to producer override; will document final rule in code comments.
- Q: Is the boost a hard tier (any audited-not-ready outranks any unaudited non-critical) or a modest priority-relative nudge? — Answer (seed intent): Hard tier — "ahead of any item (other than critical) that have no audit" indicates tier, not relative nudge. Final: implement as tiered ordering (or equivalent large numeric boost >2000).

## Summary
Extend `computeScore` + `sortItemsByScore`/`getAllOrderedByScore`/`reSort` and `selectBySortIndex` to apply a hard audit-not-ready tier second only to `critical` via batch audit map + freshness check.

## Acceptance Criteria

2. `readyToClose===true`, absent, or stale (`auditedAt < updatedAt`) audits add zero boost.
3. No non-critical audited item outranks a `critical` item (hard boundary; Critical Group in `src/commands/grouping.ts` unchanged).
4. No per-item N+1 audit queries in hot loop — `sortItemsByScore`/`reSort` builds `Map<id,AuditResult>` once per call (EdgeCache pattern); `selectBySortIndex` fallback uses same map or batch `getAllAuditResults`. `wl next` / `reSort` performance not regressed on large datasets.

Thread `Map<string,AuditResult>` through `sortItemsByScore`/`getAllOrderedByScore`/`reSort`.

## Goal

Fix the freshness clock so that post-audit comments do not invalidate audits.

## Problem

`wl comment add` calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` which updates `updatedAt`.
The `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` check in icons.ts returns false when
`auditedAt <= updatedAt - 60s`, so a comment added after the audit makes it
appear stale.

## Proposed solution

Option (c) - atomic audit persistence: `wl audit-set` (and `wl update --audit-text`)
should atomically set `updatedAt = auditedAt` (or `updatedAt >= auditedAt`) when
recording an audit. This ensures that immediately after an audit, the freshness
check always passes, regardless of subsequent comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl audit-set` sets updatedAt = auditedAt (or later) atomically with the audit record
- [ ] `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically
- [ ] After audit, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true immediately
- [ ] No race window where a read between audit-set and display sees stale data

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `saveAuditResult` method
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` command
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `wl update --audit-text` command
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh` function

The `audit_pr.py` `append_audit_comment()` function writes the full audit

- The audit verdict lives in the audit record (audit_results table)
- The implement skill reads the audit record, not comments

# Sprint Complete: Auto-Disable Dispatch & Ship Banner

## Problem statement

When all work items in the current sprint have been completed or reviewed (i.e., completed/in_review count >= the browseItemCount setting), the herdr extension should automatically disable downtime dispatching and display a green banner prompting the operator to ship.

## Users

- **Sprint lead / operator**: Sees a clear visual signal when the sprint is done and knows they can ship.
- **Downtime worker**: Stops wasting compute resources dispatching work when there's nothing left to do.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Auto-disable dispatch**: When `completed + in_review` item count >= `browseItemCount` setting, the downtime worker automatically disables dispatching (writes the disable marker, same mechanism as the `d` shortcut).
2. **Green sprint-complete banner**: A green-background, white-text banner replaces the help text below the item list displaying: `Sprint Complete, hit S to ship`.
3. **Re-enable on new items**: When new work items arrive (completed/in_review count drops below `browseItemCount`), the disable marker is removed and the banner disappears, restoring normal behavior.
4. **Banner only when sprint complete**: The sprint-complete banner is shown ONLY when the condition is met AND the help text is enabled (`showHelpText: true`); it does not interfere with code-freeze banners.
5. **All tests pass**: Full project test suite passes with new changes.
6. **Related documentation updated**: Code comments and any relevant docs reflect the new behavior.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed**: If the item count query fails, default to NOT auto-disabling (conservative).
- **Non-blocking**: The auto-disable must not crash the TUI or block normal operation.
- **Marker reuse**: Use the existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` marker file mechanism — no new persistence mechanism.
- **Banner placement**: Banner replaces the help text footer area (same chrome row budget accounting as code-freeze banners).

## Existing state

- The `browseItemCount` setting (default 20) controls how many items are displayed.
- The downtime worker already has a disable-marker mechanism (`.herdr-downtime-disabled`) used by the `d` shortcut.
- Code-freeze banners already render above the item list with proper chrome row accounting.
- The help text footer is rendered below the list and is gated by `showHelpText`.
- Completed/in_review items are tracked via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`.

## Desired change

- Add a completion-check hook that runs on each list refresh and worker tick.
- When the completion condition is met: write the disable marker, suppress the help text footer, and render the green banner.
- When the condition clears: remove the disable marker, restore the help text, and remove the banner.
- The banner text includes "hit S to ship" referencing the existing `S` shortcut for ship confirmation (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Add completion check logic to the worker tick loop; wire auto-disable into the existing marker mechanism.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add `sprintComplete` boolean parameter to the renderer; render green banner in place of help text when active.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-disable-marker.ts` — Reuse existing marker write/remove functions; add a `sprintCompleteMarkerExists` check if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Add `fetchCompletedItemCount()` helper to count completed/in_review items.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `browseItemCount`).

## Related work

- Code-freeze banners: `WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY` — similar banner rendering pattern.
- Disable marker: `WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE` — existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` mechanism.
- Ship confirmation dialog: `WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY` — the `S` shortcut the banner references.
